findings.issue: The checked-in manifest hashes LF bytes, but core.autocrlf=true checks out all four bound artifacts as CRLF. A clean Windows checkout returns Worker 503 and the existing Worker test fails. Pin the bound artifact checkout bytes and exercise both Git newline modes.

Python's stable evidence projection differs from the Worker: missing item freshness falls back to UNKNOWN instead of source freshness, and evidence IDs use code-point ordering instead of localeCompare. Valid publications built by this CLI can therefore be rejected with a release binding mismatch.

The production verifier never validates release identity/schema fields and only binds health/publication receipts. Tampered code_sha, evidence_catalog_hash or built_at and a different capabilities/search release are all accepted as hash_binding SUCCESS.

The verify command validates only internal schema/identity, so changing any served artifact bytes leaves RELEASE_MANIFEST_OK. Reuse the builder and validate_binding against the manifest's sibling publication files.

The manifest is built before source-policy prebuild synchronization, while the CI display-cap regression rewrites feed/brief without rebuilding it. Both lifecycle paths leave stale raw-byte bindings and fail the Worker regression or shipped query surface.

needs-human: code_sha is copied from Pages and worker_version is a fixed protocol label, so this binding cannot attest the code actually deployed to Cloudflare. Confirm whether issue #62 requires independent Worker deployment identity and define that contract before changing the API/deployment flow.

summary: Fixed five release-binding defects with failing-then-passing regressions: checkout bytes, evidence projection parity, production verification, local artifact verification, and workflow ordering. Git Bash npm run check passed (576 tests passed, 0 failed, 1 PostgreSQL test skipped), including the production build; an isolated CI display-cap replay also returned Worker HTTP 200. needs-human: define independent Worker deployment attestation; no live deployment, canary or human-evaluation acceptance is claimed.
